text:
marta: Quick sync — ran a new "rampbench" combining replay traces + synthetic spike to validate warmup + autoscale behavior. posting raw notes and a lightweight repro.

izzy: please drop raw numbers, TL;DR. was this apples-to-apples with previous runs?

marta: TL;DR — two surprises: 1) KV cache priming caused a 20–40% higher p95 token latency during scale-up windows; 2) batch-handoff threshold change from 128->64 reduced coldstart tail but increased CPU busy time and burned burst credits faster. not apples-to-apples until we pin kernel selection and quant states.

pete: can you paste the harness command? want to reproduce locally.

marta: sure:\n```\n./rampbench --replay /mnt/traces/prod_week1 --synthetic seq=512:rate=400 --mix 50:50 --duration 30m --kv-prime 60s --kernels auto\n```\n
simon: did you force kernel selection? auto can pick fused-attn-v2 which behaves differently on short vs long sequences.

marta: not in the first run. second run pinned `--kernels fused-attn-v1` and `--quant q4_0` to compare.

kevin: numbers from run1 (auto kernels):
- p50 token latency: 12ms
- p95 token latency: 92ms (during scale windows spiked to ~140ms)
- tokens/sec sustained: 9.2k
- burst credits consumed: 85% of pool allotment within 6m

izzy: Oof. which part of the spike correlated with KV miss rate?

marta: KV miss rate jumped from 5% baseline to ~38% immediately after each scale event. priming window was ~45–70s.

qa-bot: regression check: compared to baseline-bench-2025-11, p95 increased by +32% under mixed load.

pete: thought autoscaler uses ramp-up policy w/ reserved warm slots — was this a dedicated pool or hosted?

marta: Dedicated pool, small (4 GPUs). autoscaler policy: conservative ramp (1->2 GPUs in 60s) with burst credits to allow sudden bursts. problem is new instances come online without KV warmup, causing downstream model kernels to pay KV load penalty.

simon: so the perf regression comes from two interacting factors: kernel choice + KV priming. When kernel switches to fused-attn-V2, it reduces per-token compute but is more sensitive to KV read latency.

kevin: iirc, fused-attn-V2 uses a streaming path that overlaps KV fetch but assumes <2ms KV latency. when that assumption is violated, context switching kills throughput.

izzy: actionable?

marta: short-term: change rampbench to pre-warm KV for N seconds before accepting traffic and add a warm-pool handshake. also experiment with lowering batch-handoff threshold further to 48 for coldstart windows.

pete: can we avoid burning burst credits? suggestion: gradual batch ramp + micro-batching during first 90s to keep payload below burst threshold.

kevin: note—micro-batching hurts p50 but reduces p95 and burst consumption. we should quantify cost delta (tokens/sec vs $/token). add cost metric to rampbench.

infra-bot: scheduled a replay run with `kv-prime=120s` and `--batch-handoff=48` at 2025-11-03T18:30Z on dedicated-pool-staging-4. job id rb-1855-01.

marta: results from infra run (kv-prime=120s, handoff=48, kernels pinned fused-attn-v1):
- p50 token latency: 16ms
- p95 token latency: 68ms
- tokens/sec sustained: 8.3k
- burst credits consumed: 22% in 30m
- KV miss rate after scale: 9%

izzy: that looks way better for p95 and credits, but p50 regressed a bit. acceptable trade for SLOs.

simon: we should also add kernel-selection determinism to the autoscaler: when scaling up, pin to the kernel family that has graceful degradation under KV slowness. maybe prefer attn-v1 for initial 2 minutes.

pete: this raises a test methodology item: all apples-to-apples runs must fix (1) kernel, (2) quant, (3) kv cache state policy, (4) batch-handoff threshold, (5) pool size. otherwise differences are conflated.

kevin: agreed. and add a metric: "KV priming debt" = area under KV miss-rate curve for first 3 minutes after scale. that quantifies warmup cost.

marta: action items: \n- [ ] pete: add `kv-prime` and `batch-handoff` knobs to rampbench UI + add cost metric (due EOD)\n- [ ] simon: prototype kernel-pin policy in autoscaler (prefer attn-v1 for first 120s after scale) (due next Tues)\n- [ ] izzy: run a matrix of (kernels=[v1,v2], handoff=[64,48,32], kv-prime=[60,120,180]) on staging dedicated pools and upload CSVs (due Fri)\n- [ ] kevin: add "KV priming debt" to perf dashboard + correlate with burst credit consumption (due Thu)

qa-bot: created checklist issue #573 on board "runtime-warmup" with the tasks above.

marta: also note for docs: mention that dedicated pools should optionally support a prebind + prewarm flag that seals a small number of VMs with KV primed to reduce SLO impact.

izzy: thanks — this was a solid find. if we can show reduced SLO violations with small p50 hit, we should roll to prod. :thumbsup:

kevin: will follow up with cost analysis after izzy's runs.

marta: ok closing thread — will post raw CSVs and a short writeup in the bench run ticket. feel free to DM for access to staging jobs.

infra-bot: rb-1855-01 logs uploaded to s3://rb-logs/rb-1855-01.tar.gz

pete: grabbed logs, will start local repro now.

simon: tagging runtime-owners for visibility @here

marta: thanks everyone.
